headline: Do not train yet: 3 byte-identical train/val pairs make the validation number meaningless, and 2 unparseable label rows, 2 out-of-range class ids, 2 truncated images and 2 zero-area val boxes will crash or NaN the run — fix these seven before anything else.
training_impact: As-is, a standard Ultralytics run fails dataset verification on the out-of-range class ids (13, 15 vs nc=12) and the 6-field label rows (or silently skips them, losing one val annotation); the 2 truncated train images abort the epoch mid-run; the 2 zero-width val boxes put a NaN in the IoU/loss during validation. Even if you force it through, the val mAP is inflated by 3 images the model trained on, and 17 boxes in 2 train files are in raw pixels, teaching the model to collapse boxes toward the top-left corner.

decisions.rationale: 3 val images are byte-identical (sha1-verified) to train images: val/575886541467, val/725460290497, val/963545096650. This is the answer to 'will the validation number mean anything' — no. Every metric computed on this val set is optimistic by an unknown margin and cannot be used to compare checkpoints or ship a model. Remove the 3 val images (or re-split) before training; fixing this after training means retraining.

2 rows have 6 fields instead of 5 — a trailing '0.87' that looks like a confidence score from a non-YOLO export. One is in val (val/000000440475 line 11), so it either crashes dataset scanning or silently drops a val annotation, corrupting the number you'll report. Delete the 6th field in train/000000190753 line 5 and val/000000440475 line 11.

train/000000179265 uses class id 13 and train/000000479030 uses id 15, but data.yaml defines 12 classes (0..11). Ultralytics raises on this during dataset verification — a hard stop before the first epoch. Decide whether those two boxes are real classes (then add the missing names to data.yaml, which also fixes the nc=15 mismatch) or mislabels (remap or drop the rows).

train/000000336232 and train/000000376307 are truncated and cannot be decoded (OSError: 40/42 bytes not processed). Most training loops abort the epoch on these, or skip them with a warning easy to miss in a long log. Delete both images and their label files.

2 boxes with w=0 (val/000000356248 line 11, val/000000539883 line 3). Zero-area boxes produce NaN in most IoU implementations, which propagates into the loss and ends the run — and both are in val, so they hit exactly the pass that produces your decision metric. Drop both rows.

train/000000016249 (11/11 rows) and train/000000203294 (6/6 rows) hold raw pixel coordinates — values bounded by image dimensions (max x=484 on a 500px image), not by 1.0. An export that skipped the divide-by-width/height step. Training on these 17 boxes teaches the model to collapse boxes to the top-left corner. Normalise by image size; this also resolves 17 of the 20 out-of-bounds boxes.

20 boxes outside [0,1] in 5 train files. 17 of them are the two denormalised files above (fixed by normalising); the remaining 3 in train/000000377723, train/000000455716, train/000000477227 need individual review — clip if the overflow is a rounding artifact, drop if the box is garbage. Where loaders clip silently, the model trains against a target the annotator never drew.

data.yaml declares nc=15 but lists only 12 names, while labels on disk use ids up to 15. The yaml is wrong in both directions and is the root of the class_id_out_of_range crash. Reconcile it with the actual label ids (add the missing names or remap the 2 stray boxes) in the same pass as the class-id fix.

3 train images have no label file (train/000000011197, train/00000035682, train/000000166747). Ultralytics treats them as pure background — if they actually contain objects, the model is being explicitly taught those objects are background, suppressing recall. Check the images: annotate them or create empty .txt files if they're deliberate backgrounds.

3 boxes are listed twice in the same file (train/000000259597, train/000000416991, train/000000426203). Duplicates double-count in the loss and break the one-target-per-object assumption used by NMS-free matchers. Dedupe the repeated rows.

3 boxes at 0.0005 x 0.0005 (area 2.5e-7) in train/000000069224, train/000000221754, val/000000549220. They are dropped during letterboxing, so they contribute nothing to training while inflating the apparent annotation count — one is in val, slightly skewing per-class coverage. Drop them.

3 near-identical pairs inside train (perceptual distance 0/64): train/000000031248~986903153382, train/000000511076~772403320943, train/000000555597~168567947112. They over-weight whatever scene they contain and inflate the dataset size you report. Dedupe one of each pair.
2 label files with no image (train/454315123240, train/716312134591). Never read during training — dead weight from deleted/renamed images. Delete them.

2 empty label files (train/000000127270, train/000000453841). Intentional background images are legitimate, but an unintended empty file is a silently dropped annotation. Confirm against the images; no action needed if deliberate.
